gui.analysis.mcreator_detector.why_butto: Why are MCreator mods often discouraged?
gui.analysis.mcreator_detector.why_info:
MCreator is a tool used to create Minecraft mods without programming knowledge. However, mods produced with it very often contain problematic issues compared to normally coded projects.

1) The generated code most of the time does wrapping and unwrapping for no reason
2) The generated code sometimes uses reflection without any reason
3) The generated code sometimes uses code that breaks other mods (world generation is an example)
4) The generated code uses sets of classes, nested classes, annotations and similar structures that often make no sense whatsoever
5) The generated code does not follow correct Forge or Fabric practices
6) The generated code is sometimes completely unreadable
7) What happens if you crash? Or if you need to do something MCreator doesn't know how to do?

gui.privacy.crash_assistant_privacy_poli:
Crash Assistant

Crash Assistant is a Minecraft mod that processes your personal data (such as logs) entirely locally on your PC, limited to what is necessary to provide the functionality described in the $LINK.CRASH_ASSISTANT$. Crash Assistant itself is entirely client-side—it has no servers and never receives a copy of your logs. If you don't want Crash Assistant to process your personal data even locally, close it and remove it from the mods folder. Crash Assistant is created and operated by Daniil Averin (KostromDan) — the data controller. You can contact me on my $LINK.CRASH_ASSISTANT_DISCORD$ in the crash-assistant channel or send a direct message to @KostromDan. If you want to use e-mail, you can contact me at kostromdanlegal@gmail.com. Furthermore, according to §77 GDPR, you have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority if you believe that the processing of your personal data is illicit. The following sections describe the log-upload functionality provided by Crash Assistant.

gnomebot.dev

Because the mobile UI of mclo.gs can be inconvenient, Crash Assistant—by default—wraps the returned URL through gnomebot.dev (e.g. https://mclo.gs/X → https://gnomebot.dev/paste/mclogs/X). You can disable this behaviour in the config. Currently enabled: $GNOMEBOT_ENABLED$ gnomebot.dev is an open-source online log viewer; it fetches data from mclo.gs, displays it with convenient formatting, and caches the paste in RAM for five minutes after the last access before discarding it. gnomebot.dev is created and operated by Kristiāns Micītis (Latvian Modder). You can contact him on his $LINK.LAT_DISCORD$. We (Crash Assistant) are completely independent from Kristiāns Micītis, operator of the gnomebot.dev service; we only wrap links (we do not send logs) through them. Until you share the copied link and someone opens it—or you open it yourself—they won’t know your log exists.

mclo.gs

Logs are uploaded only when you explicitly click one of the "Upload" buttons, and they are sent using secure (HTTPS) methods directly to mclo.gs, a log-sharing service operated by Aternos GmbH (Germany). Before publishing, mclo.gs automatically tries to redact sensitive information—such as access tokens, IP addresses, or computer usernames—to keep your log safe to share. However, mclo.gs cannot guarantee that this always works. This is not anonymising! Only data that can be used to harm you is attempted to be removed. Minecraft usernames, UUIDs, hardware details and other information that may be personal are retained, as this often helps determine the cause of a crash. If you believe any information is being retained unnecessarily and is not serving a legitimate interest in the uploading and sharing of Minecraft logs, please contact them. Any log uploaded to mclo.gs is stored on their servers for up to 90 days after the last access. After that, the log is deleted automatically. Complete information on retention periods, access rights, data redaction, contact details, and your GDPR rights — such as log erasure, data access, correction, restriction, portability, objection, and the right to complain — is available in their $LINK.MCLOGS_PRIVACY_POLICY$. We (Crash Assistant) are completely independent from Aternos GmbH, operator of the mclo.gs service; we only use their API to help you share your logs.

Consent Reset

To withdraw your consent, open the menu $LANG.gui.menu.privacy$ → $LANG.gui.menu.privacy.reset_consent$ at any time. Warning: withdrawing your consent only revokes permission to upload logs. You will need to grant consent again before uploading logs in the future. This action does not remove logs that have already been uploaded to mclo.gs; you must contact them directly for deletion. Also, this action does not interrupt an already started uploading process. If you want to interrupt it, close Crash Assistant instead.

Consent Validity

By clicking Accept in the dialog before uploading a log, you give your consent to the processing of your data for the purpose of uploading logs. We (Crash Assistant) process your data (uploading logs) only on the basis of your freely given consent. Uploading logs is completely voluntary; declining to upload them will not affect Crash Assistant’s local functionality. If the checkbox $LANG.gui.privacy.remember_my_choice$ is selected, your consent will be stored locally on your PC in the "local/crash_assistant/local_config.json" path, relative to the folder of this modpack, and remains valid as long as that file exists or until you revoke your consent. If the checkbox is not selected, consent remains valid only until the GUI is closed or the consent is revoked. We may update this Privacy Policy. The current version is always available at the top of the Privacy Policy text in the menu $LANG.gui.menu.privacy$ → $LANG.gui.menu.privacy.logs_info$. When the mod is updated and this policy has changed, we automatically withdraw any previously given consent.

Upload Volume

You decide which logs to upload and for what purpose. We (Crash Assistant) only provide a convenient GUI for this. Clicking the $LANG.gui.upload_and_copy_link_button$ button next to a single entry sends only that specific log. Clicking $LANG.gui.upload_all_button$ sends every log listed under $LANG.gui.file_list_label$ plus the mods-difference file. The copied message may contain additional context — please review it before sharing.

warnings.atio6axx: The atio6axx "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file, is part of the AMD driver for the GPU, there's a bad version of the AMD drivers that instantly crashes on an OpenGL task. warnings.c6a: We detected signs in $LOG_FILENAME$ of missing Create mod classes, while the Create mod is currently installed. Create Update 6 was released recently, and you may have one of the following mismatches: - Create Update 5 with addons for Update 6, or - Create Update 6 with addons for Update 5. (Addons here refer to any mod that integrates with Create, including both standard addons and mods with Create compatibility.) You'll need to ensure that all Create-related mods are either from Update 5 or Update 6. Note that release dates are not a fully reliable way to determine compatibility. This may be a false alarm, so please double-check. To identify which mods are incompatible with your current version of the Create mod: Click OK, then open on top of the window $LANG.gui.menu.analysis$ -> $LANG.gui.menu.analysis.create_dependencies$. Wait for the process to finish—you'll then see a list of mods that are incompatible with the installed version of Create.
warnings.closed_by_windows: If this crash happened during game or level loading, or while closing the game, it was likely caused by pressing keys or clicking the mouse. The error "The program javaw.exe version ... stopped interacting with Windows and was closed" in $LOG_FILENAME$ means the game froze, possibly due to these actions. To avoid this, let the game load/close fully—DO NOT CLICK ANYTHING, PRESS ANY KEY, or CLICK END PROCESS. If the crash occurred during mid-gameplay, just press OK and ignore this message.
warnings.codex: Codex logs analyser found in $LINE$ of $LOG_FILENAME$ potential reason of this crash: Problem: $PROBLEM$ Solution(s): $SOLUTIONS$
warnings.codex_crash_assistant_comment: Crash Assistant comment on this issue:
warnings.codex_erroring_entity: If this happened with an unmodified modpack, consider reporting it to the modpack authors, as this shouldn't happen. To remove the erroring block or entity, you can try temporarily installing the Neruina mod. This will not fix the cause of the issue, but it will let you join the world and remove the problematic entity or block. For Forge and NeoForge, there is an alternative option: Forge: go to "world"/serverconfig/forge-server.toml ("world" being the name of your world) NeoForge: go to config/neoforge-server.toml Enable the appropriate option depending on what is erroring: Set removeErroringBlockEntities = true to remove any BlockEntity that throws an error in its update method. Set removeErroringEntities = true to remove any Entity that throws an error in its tick method.

warnings.disk_space_ended: The message java.io.IOException: There is not enough space on the disk in the $LOG_FILENAME$ file means: There wasn't enough space on the disk to complete an operation. You are running out of disk space! Clear some space to resolve the issue.
warnings.duplicated_mods: At the end of $LOG_FILENAME$, we found an error about duplicated mods: $LINE_FROM_LOG$ To fix this crash, keep only one of the mods listed above.
warnings.epic_fight_addons: We detected signs in $LOG_FILENAME$ of missing Epic Fight mod classes, while the Epic Fight mod is currently installed. There are a number of addon & integration mods for Epic Fight which do not properly declare which version of Epic Fight they are made for. Go through all Epic Fight addons or mods adding integration and make sure they are compatible with the current version of Epic Fight. This may be a false alarm, so please double-check. To identify which mods are incompatible with your current version of the Epic Fight mod: Click OK, then open on top of the window $LANG.gui.menu.analysis$ -> $LANG.gui.menu.analysis.epic_fight_addons_compatibility$. Wait for the process to finish—you'll then see a list of mods that are incompatible with the installed version of Epic Fight.
warnings.feature_order_cycle: In the $LOG_FILENAME$ we found a feature order cycle error. This happens when Minecraft detects a circular dependency in world generation features, usually caused by multiple mods adding features in conflicting orders. The error typically occurs when you have multiple mods that modify world generation, like biome or structure mods, or any other worldgen features. To fix this issue, you can install the Feature Recycler mod which specifically addresses this problem: $LINK.FEATURE_RECYCLER$ This lightweight mod prevents crashes between world generation mods by resolving feature order conflicts automatically. While installing this mod will solve the problem, it is only a bandaid fix. You should report this issue to the authors of the conflicting mods.
warnings.gpu_driver_issue: The $PROBLEMATIC_FRAME$ "Problematic frame" in $LOG_FILENAME$ is part of the GPU driver. To fix it, follow these instructions: $LANG.warnings_common.drivers$
warnings.groovy_mod_loader_ipv6: In the $LOG_FILENAME$ we found a GroovyModLoader (GML) IPv6 connection error. The GroovyModLoader (GML) mod may fail to download from Mojang's servers through IPv6. There are couple of options to solve this: 1) Launch the game once with the -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true JVM argument 2) Disable IPv6 entirely on pc by this guide: $LINK.IPV6$ 3) Remove GML and dependent mods. Eating Animation is one mod that depends on GML.
warnings.ig7icd64: The ig7icd64 "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file is part of the Intel driver for the integrated GPU. This is caused by the integrated GPU being too old and not supported by Java itself. To fix this, try the following: 1) If you have a dedicated GPU, you need to configure your system to use it instead of the Intel integrated GPU on the CPU. Follow the steps below: $LINK.HOW_FORCE_APP_USE_DISCRETE_GPU$ 2) If you don't have a dedicated GPU and this integrated GPU is your only option, try updating your Intel Graphics Driver from here, as this sometimes helps: $LINK.INTEL_DRIVERS$ 3) If you tried to use shaders, avoid doing so, as this integrated GPU is too old to support them. Some modpacks have shaders enabled by default. Try removing the shaderpacks folder.
warnings.insufficient_memory: The There is insufficient memory... message in the $LOG_FILENAME$ file means: Your system is running out of available physical RAM or swap space. To fix this: $FIRST_PRIORITY_WARNINGS$1) Make sure your memory isn't heavily used by other running applications — check using Task Manager, and try to keep unnecessary programs closed while playing Minecraft. 2) Ensure you are using the recommended memory settings for this modpack — perhaps your Xmx value is set too high? 3) If you followed some dumb internet advices about disabling page files, revert it — that's likely the cause. Even if you have, say, 128 GB of RAM and most of it is free, Java still needs swap space to function properly. Look for instructions how to check/enable page files in the bottom of the message. 4) Check your disk space. If you're running out of it, there might not be enough space for the swap area, so you'll need to free up some space to fix the issue. 5) Sometimes, simply restarting your computer can help clear out memory and reset swap usage. 6) If you're using more than the recommended memory settings for this pack, try lowering them. 7) If none of this helps $END_RECOMMENDATIONS$ How To Check/Enable/Change Paging File Size: 1) From the Windows search button search up "Advanced System Settings" and open the first result. 2)Press the "Settings" button located under the Performance section. 3)In the new section that has opened press "Advanced" and after press the "Change" button located under the "Virtual Memory" section. 4)Check "automatically manage paging file size for all drivers" checkbox.

warnings.jemalloc: The jemalloc "Problematic frame" in $LOG_FILENAME$ indicates an issue with the jemalloc memory allocator. To resolve this, add the following argument to your JVM args: -Dorg.lwjgl.system.allocator=system
warnings.jvm: The jvm.dll "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file may result from various issues, including a hardware bug or a bug in the JVM itself. Please try the following steps in order: $FIRST_PRIORITY_WARNINGS$1) Have you seen our warning about Intel 13th and 14th‑generation processors? If you’ve experienced any system instability (BSODs, random app crashes), this is likely the cause. 2) If memory overclocking (XMP/DOCP/EXPO) is enabled, disable it, as it doesn’t seem to work well with your system and may be causing memory corruption. Look for memeory diagnostics instructions in the buttom of this message. 3) If you have done any overclocking, like downvolting or upvolting, try reverting it. 4) Apply the recommended JVM arguments for your modpack. 5) Test different Java versions or vendors, as the bug may come from the current JVM installation version or vendor. 6) Try reducing active CPU count like this, via JVM argument: -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=$HALF_OF_PROCESSORS$ 7) If none of the above helps, contact support. Memory diagnostics instructions: 1) Save this $LINK.RESULTS_OF_MEMORY_DIAGNOSTICS$. It will be needed to get results of diagnostics after reboot. 2) Press win + R to open the Run dialog box, enter mdsched and click OK. 3) In the Windows Memory Diagnostic window, click the Restart now and check for problems option. If you don’t see a popup with the results after reboot, refer to the instructions on how to view them. Please note: this test may not detect every memory issue, and it won’t confirm if the JVM crash is 100% caused by memory. Disabling memory overclocking is still the best first step.

warnings.legacy_too_many_ids: In the $LOG_FILENAME$ we found a 'too many ids' error. This error is known to happen on legacy versions because the maximum number of ids for items or blocks is limited to 4096. Installing many mods adding many items or blocks will definitely cause this issue. Solutions: 1. Install $MOD_LINK$. This mod is specifically addressed for this issue and will fix it. 2. Remove some mods adding many blocks or items. It's strongly recommended to use the first solution.

Mixin config $CONFIG$ from mod $MOD$ failed to apply because it is corrupted or missing.
Usually this means the mod is bad, has a recently released bad update, or the mod file is corrupted.
If reinstalling the mod doesn't fix it, try removing the mod.
warnings.modernifx_watchdog: At the end of $LOG_FILENAME$, we found a message from the IntegratedWatchdog about one server tick took way longer than it should have: $LINE_FROM_LOG$ If you weren’t doing something extremely slow, like using WorldEdit to change trillions of blocks, this likely means the Integrated Server has deadlocked. A deadlock happens when parts of the game are waiting on each other in a way that prevents anything from continuing — like a traffic jam where every car is blocking another. To fix this crash, check the thread dump at the end of the log. It shows which parts of the game were waiting on each other. This can be hard to understand without technical knowledge. You can try using some advanced reasoning AI tool to analyze the thread dump — it may help identify the mod causing the issue. If this happened in an unmodified modpack, please report it to the developers — it shouldn’t happen.
warnings.module_find: In $LOG_FILENAME$ we found an error about a missing package: $LINE_FROM_LOG$ This error indicates that the mod is either missing a dependency, needs a different version of a dependency, or is just broken. It's also possible that this was caused by 2 mods placing the same dependency of different versions in jarInJar. In this case, it means the mods are incompatible. You have a couple of ways to fix this crash: 1) Visit the mod page and check which dependencies are required. Try installing or updating them. 2) If the mod works alone, it's most likely a conflict with another mod. 3) If nothing helps, or you don't want to bother, simply remove the mod. Mods that require the mentioned package: $JARS$
warnings.module_resolution: In the $LOG_FILENAME$, we found an error about duplicated packages: $LINE_FROM_LOG$ This error means mods are exporting the same package to the game, while only one with the same name is allowed to be loaded. Basically, this means either the mods are the same mod or there is a dependency conflict. You have 2 ways to fix this crash: 1) [RECOMMENDED SOLUTION] Keep only one of the mods listed below. And report the issue to both mod authors. They should relocate it or use jar in jar for their dependencies. 2) [BAD BANDAID FIX] Sometimes works, sometimes not, can cause unexpected issues. Open the mod as an archive and keep folder "$PACKAGE$" only in one of the mod jars listed below. Mods containing mentioned package: $JARS$
warnings.neo_version1_20_1:

If you are playing neo, switch to forge, as neo has dropped support for 1.20.1 and focused on newer versions; It's the official recommendation from neo.

Also newer Forge builds have improved performance / are better optimised.

Currently, OptiFine is incompatible with A LOT of mods, and this crash was most likely caused by one of these issues. There is no longer a good reason to use it. Other open-source projects offer better performance, significantly improved compatibility, and full shader support. Read this article and consider switching to an alternatives: $LINK.OPTIFINE_ALTERNATIVES$ If you are playing a modpack, it's most likely already well-optimized — you just need to remove OptiFine.
warnings.out_of_memory_error: The java.lang.OutOfMemoryError message in the $LOG_FILENAME$ file means: There isn't enough memory allocated for Minecraft to continue running. $LANG.warnings_common.memory_args$ Look up the recommended memory settings for this modpack and allocate more memory. warnings.resource_location_exception: We detected signs in $LOG_FILENAME$ that your game encountered a resource location error: $LINE_FROM_LOG$. This typically happens when Minecraft tries to load a resource (such as a block, item, or texture) using a name that contains invalid characters. This is most often caused by one of the following reasons: 1) Non-English system language settings. In such cases, the resource location may include a Unicode symbol in this format: \u0131n. To fix this, add the following JVM arguments to force the game to use English locale settings: -Duser.language=en -Duser.region=US 2) A mod has incorrectly handled a resource location. Try removing the mod that added this faulty resource. It is strongly recommended to try the first solution before resorting to the second one.
warnings.rubidium:
Rubidium is an abandoned mod with numerous bugs and stability issues.
There’s no reason to use it—please switch to $LINK.EMBEDDIUM$ instead,
which is a fork that continues its development and is actively maintained.

warnings.server_config_corrupted: In the $LOG_FILENAME$ we found a serverconfig corruption error. Corrupted config: $CONFIG_FILE$ from mod: $MOD_ID$ To fix the issue, go to saves/{world_name_where_crash_happens} and delete the serverconfig folder. The problematic config will be regenerated with default settings or from the serverconfig folder in the root of the modpack on the next world join. We recommend deleting the whole serverconfig folder because this issue is known to often happen with multiple configs.

warnings.version1_21:
Minecraft version 1.21 contains security flaws, has been abandoned, and is no longer supported.
It's very likely that this crash is caused by the abandoned version. Both modloaders and mod developers
stop releasing updates for it almost immediately after version 1.21.1 was released.
It is recommended to upgrade to version 1.21.1, 1.21.4, or 1.21.5.
warnings_common.drivers: You (likely) need to update your graphics drivers in order to resolve the crash. Here's how to go about doing that! 1. Identify your graphics card Your current GPU used to run this instance of Minecraft is: $CURRENT_GPU$ if you already know skip to the next step - Open task manager - Navigate to the "Performance" tab (on Windows 11 this is the button that looks like a heart pulse) - Press the GPU 0 graph and read your GPU from the top right Note: In some cases you may see a GPU 0 and GPU 1. This means your CPU has its own GPU, as well as a dedicated one. You probably want GPU 1 (which is usually the better one), but you can ask staff to clarify if necessary. 2. Download your drivers from the manufacturers site Depending on what you read before, you likely need drivers from either AMD, Intel, or NVIDIA AMD: $LINK.AMD_SUPPORT$ Intel: $LINK.INTEL_DRIVERS$ NVIDIA: $LINK.NVIDIA_DRIVERS$ Note: - For NVIDIA you want to select "Game Ready Driver (GRD)" (this is the default option) for the best performance. Once installing you'd probably prefer downloading GeForce Experience, which will notify you when there's an available drivers update. - For Intel, you probably want to press "Get Started" under the "Automatically update your drivers and software", which will simplify the process and update everything automatically. - For AMD you probably want to just press "Download Windows Drivers", which will download something called AMD Adrenaline, which will update your drivers automatically. 3. Run the installation, restart your computer, and try playing MC again - At this point, hopefully your Minecraft is running. If it still does not work, contact support with report from $LANG.gui.upload_all_comment$ button.
